transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. Can you please tell me what brings you in to see me today?

Thank you. I know it doesn’t make sense, but the thought of going into any kind of medical office or having tests done scares me so much that I keep putting off appointments I really need. I'm honestly a bit embarrassed to admit how much I've been avoiding them.
Can you tell me more about what specifically scares you when it comes to medical offices or tests, is it the fear of the unknown, fear of pain, or something else?

It's hard to pin down to just one thing, but the physical act of walking into a clinic or the thought of lying inside those imaging machines triggers this intense dread. My mind immediately jumps to worst-case scenarios, even though I logically understand it is likely just a routine test or a quick check-up.
Do you experience this intense dread or anxiety in other situations beyond medical offices or tests, such as in social gatherings, public speaking, or other everyday activities?

No, not at all. As a high school teacher, I speak in public and interact with people every single day without any issue. This intense dread is strictly limited to medical settings, appointments, and procedures.
Can you describe if there was a specific event or experience in the past that you associate with the onset of this intense dread of medical offices or tests?

It really started about thirteen months ago when I slipped on an icy curb at school and fractured my wrist, which required an ER visit. I've always had a minor discomfort with hospitals, but that specific fall and emergency room trip really triggered and crystallized this intense dread.

Do you also experience excessive worry about your health or fear of having a serious illness when you're not in a medical setting or anticipating a test, or is your anxiety primarily focused on the medical procedures and offices themselves?

No, I don't really worry about being sick when I'm at home; my anxiety is entirely focused on the medical offices and procedures themselves. The intense fear, sweating, and pounding heart are only triggered when I have to anticipate an appointment, step into a clinic, or even see a medical test on TV.
Can you clarify if your fear is specifically of the medical procedures and tests themselves, or is it more about the potential diagnosis or outcome of those tests?

While my mind does sometimes jump to worst-case scenarios, the fear is really about the physical medical environment and the procedures themselves. It's things like walking into a clinic, lying in an imaging machine, or having tests done that trigger the panic, rather than worrying about what a diagnosis might be.

You mentioned the fear is triggered by the physical medical environment and procedures, can you tell me if this fear is also present when you think about minor medical procedures, such as getting a routine vaccination or a blood draw?

Yes, absolutely, even minor things like getting a routine vaccination or a blood draw trigger that same intense fear now. Because those still require me to walk into a clinic and involve invasive elements like needles, they cause the exact same stomach-dropping dread as the larger appointments.
Does the fear of medical procedures or offices ever lead you to experience significant distress or impairment in your daily life or social relationships outside of the medical context itself?

Yes, it has caused a lot of distress because avoiding my appointments has made my back pain much worse, causing me to miss several days of work as a teacher. It also takes a huge emotional toll; when I do force myself to go, I sit in the parking lot shaking and have to call my sister just to talk me through walking through the door.

Can you tell me if your fear of medical offices or procedures is primarily driven by a fear of the procedures themselves, or if you also have a persistent fear of having a serious illness, even when you're not in a medical setting or anticipating a test?

It is definitely about the medical settings, offices, and procedures themselves rather than a constant worry about having a serious illness. I don't sit at home worrying about being sick, but my anxiety spikes immediately when I have to think about going into a clinic or lying in an MRI machine. The fear is entirely about facing those medical environments.
Can you confirm that your fear is more about the act of undergoing medical procedures or being in a medical setting, rather than a persistent fear of having an underlying serious illness?

Yes, that is absolutely correct. My fear is entirely about the physical offices, the machines, and the medical procedures themselves, rather than any worry about having a serious illness. Even just walking into a clinic for a routine, minor check-up is enough to trigger this intense dread.
